**Test image analysis:**
- Affected part: **leaf**
- Key features: Severely necrotic leaf with large brown papery tissue covering most of the surface, holes where tissue has broken apart, yellow-green coloration at margins, dry/crispy texture
- Not water-soaked or greasy (argues against Late Blight), no white powdery coating (not Powdery Mildew), no small discrete spots (not Septoria/Bacterial Speck)

**Reference comparison:**
The Early Blight reference shows a discrete dark brown lesion on an otherwise green leaf — an early stage. The test image represents a heavily advanced case where multiple large dark brown lesions have merged, consuming most of the leaf, consistent with Early Blight progressing to full-leaf necrosis. The dry papery texture, large dark brown areas (not greasy/water-soaked as in Late Blight), and the pattern of necrosis fit Early Blight best.

The dry (not greasy or water-soaked) texture argues against Late Blight. No small discrete spots to suggest Septoria, and no white powdery coating for Powdery Mildew."}
